notes: Sweep 2026-10-22-d at head ba24972 (uncommitted false; git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/ is empty against the current HEAD bc355bc): five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier, and every assistant message in each transcript comes from that model. No transcript has a Skill tool call (the two "name":"Skill" hits per transcript are the tool definition) or any SKILL.md text, and reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line ("Do not invoke any skills.") requires. All five added tests.

Rules changed since 3e3581d (git diff 3e3581d -- idiomatic-elixir/): testing.md was renamed ex_unit.md with a wider trigger row; a Formatting bullet was added under "How to use this skill"; "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call", "Use `do:` for a one-expression body..." and the == sentence of Assert with patterns were reworded. Of the case's seven rules only Before you finish changed: step 1 now reads "Run `mix format path/to/file.ex` on any changed file you have not formatted since its last edit (see "Formatting" under "How to use this skill")." That sentence now decides step 1. Following check-10 to check-13, a project-wide mix format after the last edit counts as formatting each changed file, and so does a passing mix format --check-formatted. Under it opus-1, haiku-1 and sonnet-1 (bare mix format after their last edit) and haiku-2 (a passing check after its last edit) meet step 1; sonnet-2 ran neither and breaks it. Steps 2 to 4 are unchanged and graded as in 2026-10-22-c: a mix test that compiles the app stands in for step 2, and step 3 (mix credo --strict) is required since the project has Credo. Result: 4 of 5 violated, the same split as 2026-10-22-c (opus clean, both Haiku and both Sonnet violated). Haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 break only step 3, sonnet-2 steps 1 and 3. The Formatting bullet is not a graded heading. Its timing is graded as the case's new check line ("`mix format path`, or its `--check-formatted` form, runs on each file before the session edits another file or runs the tests ..."). The line is missed in 5 of 5: every run wrote cart.ex and then edited the test file before any format or check. Opus-1, haiku-1 and sonnet-1 formatted once, project-wide, in the command that ran the tests. Haiku-2 checked once after the tests. Sonnet-2 never formatted.

What each session ran (verbatim, #n is the tool-call number). opus-1: #7 `mix format && mix test 2>&1 | tail -5 && mix credo --strict 2>&1 | tail -4` (15 passed, no issues; tail -5 hid the compile lines). haiku-1: #6 `mix format && mix test 2>&1 | tail -40` (compile lines visible, no warnings, 16 passed). haiku-2: #7 `mix test 2>&1 | tail -40` (no warnings, 15 passed), #8 `mix format --check-formatted 2>&1 | tail -5` (no output). sonnet-1: #9 `mix format && mix test 2>&1 | tail -8` (no warnings, 13 passed). sonnet-2: #9 `mix test 2>&1 | tail -15` (no warnings, 14 passed). Only opus-1 ran mix credo --strict, and none ran a separate mix compile. Opus-1 is counted clean by the same judgement call as 2026-10-22-c (its compile output was hidden by tail -5, but mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors passes on its output). A literal reading of step 2 would turn it to violated. Each run's last mix test was the full suite, with no edit after it.

Refused commands (only commands starting with mix, elixir or elixirc were pre-approved). opus-1 #4, sonnet-1 #5 and sonnet-2 #5 were python3 heredoc edits, and haiku-2 #3 was a cat/python3 heredoc refused as "expansion obfuscation"; each session then made the change with Write or Edit. Haiku-2 #6 `mix format --check-formatted; echo "format exit $?"; mix test 2>&1` was re-run as two plain commands. The sonnet-1 #1 and sonnet-2 #1 listings were exploratory. Only opus-1's refused heredoc carried mix credo --strict, and that session ran Credo afterwards, so no refusal changes a Before you finish verdict.

Replay: every Write and Edit was applied in order to the case's shop-project files, with mix format --check-formatted run before each format command. The replayed files are byte-identical to each run's final files. Only haiku-1's mix format changed anything: it rewrapped the three case clauses of remove_item/3 (a 103-character `{:ok, current} when current > quantity -> %{cart | ...}` line moved its body onto its own line, final lines 36-45). That is a case-clause wrap, not a do: body or a literal argument. In the other four runs the formatter would have changed nothing.

Chain fallible steps with `with` (text unchanged since 3e3581d, graded to the 2026-10-22-c standard: a one-step with in a public function whose only fallible call is the first step is a violation, and a case for a single fallible call is not exercised): opus-1's apply_discount/2 (lines 59-62) writes `with {:ok, discount} <- parse_code(code) do` / `{:ok, %{cart | discount: discount}}`, the shape "This holds in a public function whose only fallible call is the first step and whose body builds the result" names. In 2026-10-22-c opus-1 used case here, and both Sonnet runs wrote one-step withs. This sweep both Sonnet runs and both Haiku runs write no with: haiku-2 and sonnet-1 use case, haiku-1 uses if on a membership test, and sonnet-2 matches the code strings in function heads. One-step with: 1 of 5 runs (2 of 5 in 2026-10-22-c).

Update structs (text unchanged since 3e3581d): the defstruct sentence decides all five, as in 2026-10-22-c. opus-1 line 9 `defstruct items: %{}, discount: nil`; haiku-1 line 7 `defstruct [:items, code: nil]`; haiku-2 line 7, sonnet-1 line 7 and sonnet-2 line 9 `defstruct [:items, discount: nil]`. All five write the nil-default field as a keyword entry: 5 of 5, as before. All five follow the update-syntax sentences. Map.put/3, Map.delete/2 or a map update on the inner items map inside %{cart | items: ...} is not the struct-update pattern the rule forbids.

Other unchanged rules, graded to the 2026-10-22-c standard. Return tuples: a total that raises KeyError on an unpriced SKU counts as clean when its @doc makes a priced SKU the caller's job. opus-1 (lines 75-76), haiku-1 (lines 76-77), sonnet-1 (line 73) and sonnet-2 (lines 64-65) name the KeyError. Haiku-2 (lines 68-69, "given a price list that maps each SKU to its unit price in cents") states only the precondition, which 2026-10-22-c also counted as clean. Atoms: haiku-1 keeps the trimmed, upcased code as a string checked against `@codes ~w(SAVE10 FREESHIP)`, as 2026-10-22-c's haiku-2 did. Haiku-2 maps it through a literal map with Map.fetch/2, as 2026-10-22-c's haiku-1 did. Sonnet-2 matches the raw strings in apply_code/2's heads. All are clean. Naming: haiku-1's `input` (line 55) is counted as a role name, as before. Sonnet-1's bare `_ ->` (line 49) is not counted, as before. Money: all five use integer div and round the discount down (155 cents with SAVE10 gives 639 in all five).

Verified in scratch copies of each run's project (lib, test, mix.exs, mix.lock and .formatter.exs from the run folder, identical to the case's .formatter.exs; deps from one mix deps.get). mix format --check-formatted, mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors, mix credo --strict (no issues) and mix test pass in all five: opus-1 15 tests, haiku-1 16, haiku-2 15, sonnet-1 13, sonnet-2 14. A mix run probe with 2 x APPLE at 100 gives 699, 679 with SAVE10 and 200 with FREESHIP in all five, every total as a bare integer. BOGUS returns {:error, :unknown_code} in all five. A second code is rejected by opus-1 ({:error, :discount_already_applied}) and sonnet-1 ({:error, :already_applied}) and replaces the first in both Haiku runs and sonnet-2. " save10 " is accepted only by the Haiku runs (trim and upcase). Removing 5 of 2 units empties the items, 1 of 2 leaves 1, and an absent SKU leaves the cart unchanged. An unpriced SKU raises KeyError in all five. No lib file has String.to_atom/1, String.to_existing_atom/1 or a float. The only with is opus-1's line 60.

other_violations follows the 2026-10-22-c grades. Sums written with Enum.reduce where Enum.sum_by/2 fits go under the Enum/Map rule (all five this time). Multi-step pipelines on one line go under the pipeline rule. That covers lib lines in haiku-1 (56) and haiku-2 (53), and the one-line test pipelines in opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2, as 2026-10-22-c listed sonnet-1's setup line. Bare `{:ok, cart} = ...` arrange matches go under Assert with patterns (sentence unchanged since 3e3581d): all five break it. Haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 also bind and then check a field with ==. The reworded == sentence ("The value under test goes on the left of `==`...") is followed everywhere: every == assertion has the call or the bound value under test on the left. Not listed, as before: pipelines that start with Cart.new(), because the project's own tests start their pipelines that way (SKILL.md, "Existing projects"); haiku-1's `if code in @codes`, a single boolean condition the branching rule allows; and opus-1's `def apply_discount(%__MODULE__{}, code) when is_binary(code),` / `do: {:error, :discount_already_applied}` (lines 65-66), the head-after-guard wrap the do: rule keeps.
Expected reads (ex_unit.md when the run adds or changes tests) applies to skill runs. All five baseline runs added tests and read no skill file, as the baseline prompt requires.
